bio: Reigning world champion. Norris won the 2025 title in a three-way fight that went to the Abu Dhabi finale, and now carries the number 1.
Cool-headed and relentlessly consistent, Piastri led much of the 2025 championship and is firmly established as a title contender.
Mercedes team leader and a qualifying specialist, with wins in Canada and Singapore during 2025.
Promoted straight from F2 to replace Lewis Hamilton, the Bologna teenager took his first podium in Montreal in his rookie season.
Four-time champion (2021–2024) and the youngest race winner in history. Switches to number 3 for 2026 after losing the crown by two points.
A standout rookie season at Racing Bulls, including a podium at Zandvoort, earned Hadjar a seat alongside Verstappen.
Ferrari's homegrown star and one of the fastest qualifiers of his generation. Won his home race in Monaco in 2024.
Record holder for wins, poles and podiums, and joint record holder with seven titles. Now chasing an eighth in red.
The driver who revived his career at Williams and became a cornerstone of the team's rebuild.
Four-time race winner who brought his experience to Grove and scored Williams' first podium in years at Baku in 2025.
A fierce racer from Hastings, New Zealand, back at Racing Bulls after a brief spell at the senior team.
The only full-time rookie of 2026 and the latest product of the Red Bull junior program.
Double world champion (2005, 2006) and the most experienced driver in F1 history by race starts.
Took a podium in only his eighth start and a memorable wet pole in Turkey in 2020.
Winner of the chaotic 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix and now Haas's experienced leader.
Scored points on a surprise debut for Ferrari in Jeddah in 2024 and has grown into a regular points scorer.
Finally ended the longest wait for a podium in F1 history at Silverstone in 2025, in his 239th start.
Back-to-back F3 and F2 champion who stepped up with Sauber and continues into the Audi era.
Shock winner of the 2020 Italian Grand Prix and Alpine's team leader.
Argentina's first F1 driver in over two decades, with a huge following back home.
Six-time race winner and tyre whisperer, back on the grid after a year out to lead Cadillac's debut season.
Ten-time winner and five-time constructors' champion with Mercedes, returning to a race seat with Cadillac.
